title: Angles
description: Understanding angle facts for points, lines, triangles and quadrilaterals, and using them to find missing angles.

notes.heading: Types of Angles
notes.body: Angles are measured in degrees. An acute angle is less than 90°. A right angle is exactly 90°. An obtuse angle is between 90° and 180°. A straight angle is exactly 180°. A reflex angle is between 180° and 360°. Common mistake: calling any angle bigger than 90° obtuse — it must also be smaller than 180°.

notes.heading: Angles on a Straight Line and Around a Point
notes.body: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°. If you know one angle, subtract it from 180° to find the other. Angles around a point add up to 360°. Example: if two angles around a point are 110° and 95°, the third angle is 360° − 110° − 95° = 155°. Always check that your answer is sensible.

notes.heading: Vertically Opposite Angles
notes.body: When two straight lines cross, the angles opposite each other are equal. They are called vertically opposite angles. For example, if one angle is 70°, the angle directly opposite it is also 70°. The other pair of opposite angles will also be equal to each other. Look for the X shape made by the crossing lines.

notes.heading: Angles in a Triangle
notes.body: The three interior angles inside any triangle always add up to 180°. If you know two angles, add them and subtract from 180° to find the missing angle. Example: a triangle has angles 55° and 65°. The third angle is 180° − 55° − 65° = 60°. This works for every triangle, whether it is equilateral, isosceles or scalene.

notes.heading: Angles in a Quadrilateral
notes.body: The four interior angles inside any four-sided shape add up to 360°. To find a missing angle, add the three known angles and subtract from 360°. Example: a quadrilateral has angles 90°, 100° and 80°. The missing angle is 360° − 90° − 100° − 80° = 90°. A rectangle uses this rule because 4 × 90° = 360°.

flashcards.definition: An angle that is smaller than 90°.

flashcards.example: The corner of a piece of paper is a right angle.
Angles on a straight line add to 180°.

flashcards.definition: Angles opposite each other where two lines cross; they are equal.
flashcards.example: If one angle is 50°, the opposite angle is also 50°.

flashcards.definition: The three interior angles of a triangle add up to 180°.
The four interior angles of any quadrilateral add up to 360°.
flashcards.example: A rectangle has four 90° angles, and 4 × 90° = 360°.

questions.stem: Which of these angles is acute?
questions.explanation: An acute angle is less than 90°, so 45° is the only acute angle in the list.

questions.stem: Two angles sit on a straight line. One angle is 70°. What is the other angle?
questions.explanation: Angles on a straight line add to 180°, so the missing angle is 180° − 70° = 110°.

questions.stem: Three angles meet at a point. They are 90° and 120°. What is the third angle?
questions.explanation: Angles around a point add to 360°. Subtract: 360° − 90° − 120° = 150°.

questions.stem: Two straight lines cross. One of the angles formed is 50°. What is the vertically opposite angle?
questions.explanation: Vertically opposite angles are equal, so the opposite angle is also 50°.

questions.stem: A triangle has angles 60° and 70°. What is the missing angle?
questions.explanation: Angles in a triangle add to 180°. The missing angle is 180° − 60° − 70° = 50°.

questions.stem: A quadrilateral has angles 80°, 90° and 100°. What is the missing angle?
questions.explanation: Angles in a quadrilateral add to 360°. The missing angle is 360° − 80° − 90° − 100° = 90°.

questions.stem: Which of these is an obtuse angle?
questions.explanation: An obtuse angle is between 90° and 180°, so 95° is obtuse.

questions.stem: A right angle and a 35° angle are next to each other on a straight line. What is the remaining angle?
questions.explanation: The three angles add to 180°. So the remaining angle is 180° − 90° − 35° = 55°.

questions.stem: A triangle has angles 40°, x and x. What is the value of x?
questions.explanation: The angles add to 180°. The two equal angles total 180° − 40° = 140°, so each is 70°.

questions.stem: A quadrilateral has angles 110°, 80°, 70° and x. What is x?
questions.explanation: Quadrilateral angles add to 360°. So x = 360° − 110° − 80° − 70° = 100°.

questions.stem: Which of these angles is reflex?
questions.explanation: A reflex angle is between 180° and 360°, so 200° is reflex.

questions.stem: Two angles around a point are 130° and 80°. What is the remaining angle?
questions.explanation: Angles around a point add to 360°. The remaining angle is 360° − 130° − 80° = 150°.
